headline: Australia's coach admits Bangladesh wins first Test in Australia
summary: Coach Andrew McDonald admits the team failed to maintain standards after a dominant performance by Bangladesh in Darwin.
details: Bangladesh has achieved a historic first Test victory on Australian soil in Darwin, dominating the match throughout the most of the three-and-a-half-day game.
Australia struggled significantly, falling 226 runs behind after their first innings of 198 runs. In the second innings, they were only able to set a target of 57 runs for Bangladesh.
Bangladesh chased down the target, winning the match by 9 wickets, with only one wicket lost in the pursuit of 57 runs.
Australian head coach Andrew McDonald expressed disappointment, stating that scoring under 500 runs across two innings on such a pitch was a failure to maintain their standards.
The defeat has sparked calls for change in the Australian squad, with former cricketer Ricky Ponting suggesting changes to the opening and number three positions.
Other former cricketers have urged the national team to integrate more youth, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 years old among the Australian players in the match.
Coach McDonald acknowledged the pressure for change but maintained that the current players still have a lot of cricket left in them, despite the ongoing discussions about squad balance.
caption:
A historic first for Bangladesh! 🇧🇩

Australia's coach admits they were outplayed in a historic Test win for Bangladesh.

Bangladesh has achieved a historic first Test victory on Australian soil in Darwin, dominating the match throughout the most of the three-and-a-half-day game.

Australia struggled significantly, falling 226 runs behind after their first innings of 198 runs. In the second innings, they were only able to set a target of 57 runs for Bangladesh.

Bangladesh chased down the target, winning the match by 9 wickets, with only one wicket lost in the pursuit of 57 runs.

Australian head coach Andrew McDonald expressed disappointment, stating that scoring under 500 runs across two innings on such a pitch was a failure to maintain their standards.

The defeat has sparked calls for change in the Australian squad, with former cricketer Ricky Ponting suggesting changes to the opening and number three positions.

Other former cricketers have urged the national team to integrate more youth, noting that only Cameron Green was under 30 years old among the Australian players in the match.

Coach McDonald acknowledged the pressure for change but maintained that the current players still have a lot of cricket left in them, despite the ongoing discussions about squad balance.

headline_marked: Cabinet approves draft to [[RAB to be abolished]], replaced by SRB
headline: Cabinet approves draft to RAB to be abolished, replaced by SRB
summary: The Rapid Action Battalion will be replaced by the Special Response Battalion (SRB) under the new 'Special Response Battalion Act, 2026'.
details: The Bangladesh Cabinet has approved the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion Act, 2026', following vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.
Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and a specialized unit called the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as part of the police force will be established.
The Act includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to handle citizen complaints and internal conflicts among unit members.
All personnel, orders, powers, authorities, facilities, funds, assets, accounts, records, and other related assets of RAB will be transferred to the SRB.
Existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations until new rules are formulated.
caption:
RAB is set to be abolished. A new specialized police unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will take its place.

The Bangladesh Cabinet has approved the draft of the 'Special Response Battalion Act, 2026', following vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division.

Under this new law, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) will be abolished and a specialized unit called the Special Response Battalion (SRB) as part of the police force will be established.

The Act includes provisions for a multi-party grievance redressal committee to handle citizen complaints and internal conflicts among unit members.

All personnel, orders, powers, authorities, facilities, funds, assets, accounts, records, and other related assets of RAB will be transferred to the SRB.

Existing RAB departmental proceedings rules will remain in effect with necessary adaptations until new rules are formulated.
